title: surface-gpu quarter-turn rotation
description:
The M5 surface-gpu path was upright-only: the dispatcher's gate
required effectiveDeg == 0, so a vertical clip (3840x2160 sensor
frame, upright 2160x3840) fell back to encoder-input=surface and
paid the CPU rotate plus the writer's own copy on every frame.

The rotation now rides the session's encoder blit itself. The
developed texture stays linear sdr-rgb; BLIT_FRAGMENT (the shared
source the writer's Surface mode also compiles, and which never
sets uRotation) gains an int uRotation uniform defaulting to 0 in
GLSL, plus a texture-coordinate fold that reproduces
rotateRgb888's quarter-turn index math in-shader:

  0:   src = (g.x, uSize.y-1-g.y)
  90:  src = (uSize.x-1-g.y, uSize.y-1-g.x)
  180: src = (uSize.x-1-g.x, g.y)
  270: src = (g.y, g.x)

with uSize carrying the SOURCE dims and the session swapping the
destination viewport to (h,w) for 90/270. Because the uniform
defaults to 0, t
changed: feat: encoder blit applies quarter-turn rotation
